MAZDOCK: Zero-debt defence-shipbuilding PSU. FY26 revenue +12%, and Q1 FY27 PAT jumped ~21% with margins expanding; analysts model ~20% earnings CAGR and ~28% ROE. Watch: order book slipped to ~₹20,500cr as flagship warship projects complete — the next leg depends on new large contracts (P75I, LPD) and the Colombo Dockyard / Tuticorin commercial push.
CASTROLIND: Near debt-free lubricants leader — ~43% ROE, ~4.5% dividend yield. Q2 CY26 revenue +25%, PAT +43%, EBITDA +41%, and the interim dividend was raised to ₹6.25. Targeting ~2x market volume growth via rural + premium expansion. Overhang: parent bp is selling its global Castrol business to Stonepeak.
ATUL: Near debt-free specialty-chemicals maker. Q1 FY27 net profit nearly doubled (+92%) on +25% revenue, led by Performance Chemicals (+34%); a new ₹167cr downstream-integration capex adds high-margin capacity. Rides the 12–18% specialty-chemicals sector tailwind — key risk is US tariffs / global oversupply.
ORIENTELEC: CK Birla consumer-electricals (fans, lighting, appliances), net-cash balance sheet. Q1 FY27 revenue +23.5% and PAT +80%, with the premium BLDC-fan range +36%. Premiumisation plus a cost program is driving the turnaround; watch commodity-led gross-margin pressure.
MUKANDLTD: Bajaj-group specialty alloy steel. The real story is deleveraging — large land-sale monetisation (Dighe ₹555cr, Kalwa ₹112cr) cut debt sharply and earned an ICRA upgrade (JV debt/EBITDA ~0.9x). Honest caveat: recent profits lean heavily on one-off land gains and FY26 core operating cash flow was negative — Q1 FY27 results (12 Aug) reveal the true core trend. More a balance-sheet-repair play than an earnings-growth one.
